title: SR2021 No6 2026 anaerobic-digestion installation emissions QA controls

sources.title: SR2021 No 6: anaerobic digestion facility, including use of the resultant biogas – installations

facts.source_fact: SR2021 No6 is for a Part A anaerobic-digestion installation with treatment capacity over 100 tonnes per day and no more than 100,000 tonnes accepted per year.
The standard rules apply to England.
The rules were updated on 26 February 2026.
An operator can use the standard rules permit only where the activity meets the rules and the generic risk assessment can be managed.
The 2026 update changed Activity 4 for treating biogas and biomethane.
The 2026 update added conditions and a table for captured, treated and stored carbon dioxide.
The 2026 update added accidental release of carbon dioxide to the generic risk assessment.
Where CCR or HCR conditions were stated in the application, the operator must keep a site-specific decarbonisation readiness report.
The decarbonisation readiness report must be reviewed and updated at intervals not exceeding 2 years.
The Environment Agency must be notified when the type of technical assessment changes for plant covered by the readiness report.
Point-source emissions to air, water or land are not allowed except from listed sources and emission points.
Point-source emissions must be identified on a site plan.
Combustion-plant stacks burning biogas are monitored annually over a minimum one-hour periodic reference period.
Monitoring equipment, techniques, personnel and organisations must use MCERTS certification or accreditation where available unless otherwise agreed.
The listed annual stack limit for oxides of nitrogen on combustion plant burning biogas is 500 mg/m3 using EN 14792.
The listed annual stack limit for carbon monoxide is 1400 mg/m3 using EN 15058.
The listed total volatile organic compounds limit, including methane, is 1000 mg/m3 using EN 12619.
Gas pressures must be monitored and recorded and pressure-relief and vacuum systems inspected.
Emissions of unburnt biogas must be minimised.
Operators need contingency measures for reduced grid demand and venting or flaring gas for disposal purposes is not permitted.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve the cited rule without broadening it.
Attach permit type, capacity and activity scope.
Attach the 2026 rule version and future-dated limits where relevant.
Carry emission point, method, standard and frequency provenance.
Do not convert permit controls into parcel-level measured emissions.
